scope: Branch-cleanup CLI only; separate from scientific consolidation validation.
coverage: Wrong URL or authenticated repository identity refusal
Changed, removed, added, renamed, or redirected manifest entries refusal
Missing or advanced candidate heads refusal
Missing, changed, or incorrectly peeled preservation refs refusal
Default, protected, or unknown-protection candidate refusal
Open PR source or target candidate refusal
Post-delete verification of candidates and observed retained refs
Default dry-run makes no push and creates an exclusive append-only receipt
Inherited repository-scoping Git environment and injected config overrides removed; transport/authentication environment preserved
Real local bare Git remote: concurrent candidate update causes leased atomic deletion to fail without deleting either candidate
Real local bare Git remote: successful atomic deletion removes only requested heads and preserves tag
review_fix: Removed inherited GIT_DIR and related repository scope, GIT_CONFIG file overrides, and injected GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS/COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n from child command environments.
usage_requirements: Python 3.10+, git, and GitHub CLI are installed.
gh is authenticated to github.com with repository read access.
Native git transport is independently authenticated for fetching and, for --apply, pushing; gh login alone may not configure git authentication.
Dry run is the default. --apply is the sole explicit deletion switch.
The real execution must pass fresh metadata, branch protection, open PR, full Git ref, tag peel, and commit ancestry checks.
limits: These tests did not perform a GitHub dry run or any real remote deletion.
Commit ancestry checks are implemented using fetched Git objects; full ChatBubble object fetching was not performed in this offline validation.

Atomic deletion leases guard candidate heads. Keeper refs and GitHub policies are rechecked immediately before deletion and retained refs are checked afterward; changes to those refs or policies cannot be atomically leased by this deletion-only push.
An apply attempt with uncertain result or failed post-check retains the temporary bare object repository and writes its location to the receipt for recovery; it does not claim rollback.
